start.text: At the top of the ladder you hear them before you see them: two old men by the lodge, and neither of them talking. Aldous got up ahead of you. He's on a plank seat somebody's dragged out in front of the lantern bench, his bag between his feet, breathing like a man who's climbed a ladder for the first time in thirty-one years.
start.note: Day 99 (ridge arrival event thornwold_two_keepers): Aldous's sorry in person — the Lamp's promise of Day 47, 'the day the lanes run with nobody counting'.

start.text: Wynn has put the chisel down. The hood is back, and the grey eyes are on the door-warden as if he were weather coming in.
The Lamp has put the chisel down. The hood turns to the door-warden and stays there.

unnamed.text: The Lamp lifts one black hand off the bench.
Don't. It's paid. The Book's keeping it.
Whatever you were going to call me, I put it somewhere. Leave it there.
...Lamp, then. It suits you better than it should.

sorry.text: I'm sorry. For all of it. For the door, and the coal you carried down past me, and thirty winters of not coming up a ladder to say so.
A door-warden isn't the door. I said I'd tell you that myself.
I said I'd tell you the day the lanes run with nobody counting.

lit.text: It turns on the bench and looks east, past the shoulder of the spine, to where the Hearthspire stands gold on the edge of the sea.
Bram Kettle's stopped notching it. So I reckon that's today.
It took the hand first. The one that carried it.
It always does. That's why we wrote the names down.

released.text: Nothing out east to count. Nothing in the box worth breaking. And something sits up with me at this bench of a night that doesn't need a sliver to see by.
The far end of the plank seat, past Aldous, is warm. He puts his hand to it, and takes it away.
They came out. It's not the same. So I reckon that's today.

box.text: It lifts the lid of the iron box. The last of the Spire's midwinter coal is in there, the size of a thumbnail, cold down one side.
I kept it for the four. They came home along the ridge without it.
I kept it for the four.
At midwinter somebody goes up for a coal and comes back asked. This can go out now. I'd like you to watch it go, Wren. You watched the rest.
It's going out anyway. Let it go out in company.
Aldous watches it. It takes a long while, and neither of them says anything, and it goes out.

novice.text: Aldous looks at you, and then at the bench beside him.
The seventh light on the east landing, that last winter. It was them. I still can't find the face. I've taken their word.
The grey eyes come round to you and stay, the way they'd stay on a coal deciding whether it's caught.
Keep one back this year, Keeper Sallow.
I kept one back. It kept this ridge lit thirty winters, and the colliers' road, and your stair. I said I'd thank whoever it was. Thank you.
And I said I'd ask how you knew my name.
You don't know. You tell it so.
No. Well. The stair kept its own counsel. It always did.
I don't know what that is to me. It sits like a thing I put down somewhere and can't go back for.

bench.text: I thought I was the only one of us who ran and lived.
You ran. I stayed and broke a coal. We both lived. It's a long bench.
